title: A build typo, a pagination migration and an export that skips rows
source: Scripted by the assistant for the follow-up round; not a recorded OpenCode session. Turns 2, 4, 6 and 7 are terse follow-ups whose tier depends on the earlier turns.

turns.user: Why does npm run build print "Unknown option --minfy"?
turns.assistant: The build script in package.json passes --minfy; the bundler's option is --minify.
turns.label: small

turns.assistant: Changed --minfy to --minify in package.json; the build runs cleanly.
turns.label: small

turns.user: Convert GET /orders to use the new paginate() helper instead of its own offset and limit handling.
turns.assistant: Converted /orders and its tests. Eleven other list endpoints still hand-roll offsets: /customers, /invoices, /products, /refunds, /shipments, /suppliers, /warehouses, /users, /audit, /coupons and /returns.
turns.label: medium

turns.user: do the same for the rest
turns.assistant: Converted the remaining eleven endpoints to paginate() and updated their tests; all pass.
turns.label: medium

turns.user: Since that change, the nightly export sometimes misses a few orders, but only when it overlaps the cleanup job that deletes old drafts. Work out why.
turns.assistant: paginate() pages by offset, so rows deleted by the cleanup job shift later pages and the export skips rows. Wrapped the export in a REPEATABLE READ transaction so every page sees one snapshot.
turns.label: large

turns.assistant: The snapshot is not used: paginate() takes a new connection from the pool for each page, outside the transaction. The alternative is keyset pagination on (created_at, id), which does not depend on a snapshot.
turns.label: large

turns.assistant: Switched the export to keyset pagination on (created_at, id) and added a test that deletes rows mid-export; no orders are missed.
turns.label: large
